newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - April 28.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - April 28.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

GREENSBORO, North Carolina - In a major blow to the tobacco industry, a federal judge rules that the Food and Drug Administration can regulate sales and labelling of cigarettes, but that it has no authority over advertising.

OTTAWA - A new anti-tobacco law which will restrict tobacco advertising and ban vending machine sales of tobacco is being introduced in Canada. The law will also restrict tobacco company sponsorship of sporting and cultural events.

PARIS - Advertising agency McCann-Erickson has won the advertising account for oil company Esso, part of Exxon Corp, in Britain, Argentina and Uruguay. The agency already manages the Esso budget in 52 countries.

LONDON - French soccer star Eric Cantona, the striker for England's Manchester United football club who has already appeared in advertisements for Eurostar and Nike, is to star in a TV ad for Liptonice, a sparkling iced tea, ad agency J. Walter Thompson says.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

NEW YORK - Cablevision, which owns a cable system with 2.8 million subscribers, sports teams and an array of entertainment assets, declined to comment on a New York Times report about possible bids for the company.

NEW YORK - U.S. television broadcasters will argue in a government filing that News Corp's proposed Sky satellite-television venture should have to carry the on-air signals of all local stations, the Wall Street Journal says.
PARIS - ABSat, the digital satellite television service of AB Productions, aims to have about 75,000 susbcribers at the end of the year against about 5,000 now, as the result of a major campaign.
TOKYO - Hitachi Ltd says that it, Fujitsu Ltd and NEC Corp are joining forces to develop infrastructure for electronic shopping over the Internet.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
LONDON - Unilever says it has agreed to sell its Helene Curtis professional haircare products business in Japan to Shiseido Co Ltd for an undisclosed sum.

SYDNEY - New Zealand-based brewer Lion Nathan is to concentrate on regional beer brands as it aims to claw back market share in Australia from the popular national brands of rival Foster's Brewing Group Ltd. "We think an enormous strength of ours is that regionality, or parochialism, is important in the decision-making when you buy beer," says a spokesman.
FRANKFURT - Ferdinand Piech, head of German carmaker Volkswagen, says he plans to more than quadruple the group's pre-tax profit by the end of the century by reducing the number of model bases.
SEOUL - Samsung Motors Inc, a unit of South Korea's Samsung Group, plans to export cars from mid-1998 to emerging markets, a company official says.

BEIJING - The share of imported cars in China's markets has fallen to its lowest level since the 1949 communist take-over, but imports could revive next year as domestic sales improve, the China Daily Business Weekly says

JOHANNESBURG - South Africa is suffering from an increase in smuggling from other parts of Africa which is hitting legitimate businesses. The main goods smuggled in are tobacco, alcoholic drinks, televisions and video recorders.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

TOKYO - Navigating the congested, narrow streets of Tokyo is easy compared to the headache of hunting for a place to park. But one firm is trying to change all that -- by transforming tiny pockets of land into parking lots to the delight of motorists.
LONDON - Demand for jewellery will continue to grow in the next decade in line with an expanding global economy but a repeat of the 1980s boom is unlikely, industry experts say.
ESTEPA, Spain - Spain's olive oil farmers are sizzling mad. Their age-old industry is being threatened by controversial European Union reforms to subsidies.

SOFIA - Bulgaria's growing income from big-game hunting is threatened by poachers who are driven by poverty to kill, for a few dollars' worth of meat, stags whose antlers could fetch thousands as rich hunters' trophies, says the Bulgarian Forestry Commission.
DUBAI - Dubai's month-long shopping festival generated record sales and boosted the emirate's image as the Gulf's trade and tourism centre, officials say.
